verdict_scope: Blockers to LOCAL DEV MCP TEST only. Not production admission, not an admission vote, not full verification.
method: source and evidence reading plus digest arithmetic; nothing executed, no MCP started, no build, no source edit, no VCS mutation, no paid model call
verified_ok: v8->v9 counterexample is genuine: REVISE verdict refused by v9; verdict gated twice (admission.gleam:175-176 and :215-216)
grant-equality preconditions hold on live files: reviewer session abe9bd8d != grant session 01a083d2; grant_proposal path/sha256/grant_id/target_session/target_worker all bind
same_object is a correct top-level set equality (equal length, unique keys both sides)
effect dedup sound: durable intent before dispatch, pending-without-result refuses, replay refuses non-EXECUTED

findings.title: stop line traps on errors with no effect; session cannot recover
findings.detail: Every error in the claim/attach selected block sets unresolved:True, including pure argument validation and a.lookup task_not_in_reviewed_grant, which dispatch nothing. harness_claim is then refused (:160-162); harness_attach fails because admission.gleam:307 requires an already-executing owned row; harness_reconcile routes to recover() which reads a completion-intent that was never written. Unrecoverable without a process restart.
findings.falsifier: harness_claim with plan 'uos/does-not-exist', then harness_claim with the correct plan: the second call is refused.
findings.bounded_fix: Apply the discrimination already present at :210-211 to :139/:173/:197/:202, or gate on an explicit outcome-unknown allowlist. The stop line must mean the outcome is unknown, never that a request was refused.

findings.title: dangling effect intent has no reconciliation path
findings.detail: effect() refuses forever when an intent exists without a result (correct no-retry rule), but reconcile() and recover() both read '<intent>-completion-intent.json' while effect() writes '<intent>-intent.json'. After a transport restart mid-effect the state is permanently unresolvable through the MCP surface.
findings.falsifier: Create <grant-id>-probe-intent.json with no -result.json, attach, harness_write_file intent_id probe -> unknown_effect_outcome_requires_reconciliation; harness_reconcile intent_id probe -> fails on the missing completion-intent path. No tool sequence clears it.
findings.bounded_fix: harness_reconcile should dispatch on which intent file exists; for a dangling effect intent, re-capture the scope, compare against the receipt input_manifest, and write a terminal FAILED_OR_UNVERIFIED result. Never re-execute.

findings.title: grant validity is point-in-time while task and coordinator are horizon-checked (root's temporal-authority question: CONFIRMED)
findings.detail: fence_for horizon-checks the Sa-plan lease and coordinator_deadline against now+required_ms, but validate_window only requires grant.expires_us > now with no lower bound on remaining time, and admission.fence passes no window to it. An operation may begin with 1 microsecond of grant validity left. For effects the overrun IS caught by the closing fence at operations.gleam:133 and the receipt records FAILED_OR_UNVERIFIED - but harness_write_file already replaced the file inside perform (:85), so the side effect is committed under expired authority. WORSE for harness_finish: after the 10s fence at :275 nothing revalidates the grant, so sa.complete_sa_task at :280 can commit a canonical Sa-plan completion after grant expiry with no closing fence at all.
findings.falsifier: Set expires_utc_us to now+2_000_000 (2s), attach, call harness_finish. The 10s fence passes on the task lease; the completion lands after grant expiry and no error is raised.
findings.bounded_fix: Add a required_us parameter to validate_window (grant.expires_us - now >= required_us) and have admission.fence pass {duration_ms+5000}*1000, so grant, task lease and coordinator lease share one horizon. Also add a.check(execution.grant) immediately after operations.gleam:283 so completion has a closing fence like effects do.

findings.title: frame_bound error is unreachable; an oversize frame halts the transport
findings.detail: serve_loop accepts a byte only while size < frame_limit, so the longest deliverable line is exactly 524288 bytes; handle() guards byte_size(line) <= frame_limit, and 524288 <= 524288 is True. The -32600 frame_bound branch can never be taken. serve_loop reaches the bound first and calls halt(1): the client sees EOF instead of a protocol error, and state.execution and state.unresolved die with the process, which then lands in B2.
findings.falsifier: Send one 600 KB line. Expected -32600 frame_bound; actual process exit 1 with 'harness: frame bound' on stderr.
findings.bounded_fix: On exceeding the bound, drain to the next newline and hand the handler a sentinel producing the -32600 reply instead of halting.

findings.title: review task binding never checked; a review of a completed task activates the grant
findings.detail: validate_review binds grant_id, target_session, target_worker, proposal path and digest, and requires reviewer.session_id != grant.session. It never reads reviewer.task_id. The live v9 review carries reviewer.task_id ADMISSION-REVIEW, the completed old task, and the grant validates today.
findings.falsifier: The current files: docs/reviews/20260909-1751-agy-successor-v9-grant-review.json names a completed task and admission.check returns Ok.
findings.bounded_fix: Require reviewer.task_id to name a task that is not completed in canonical Sa-plan at check time and belongs to the same plan. Trap to avoid: checking mere presence of the field is a coarser observable than the property; the value must be resolved against the store.

findings.title: harness_finish is not gated by the unresolved stop line
findings.detail: finish runs regardless of state.unresolved while write/build/test are gated. Partially mitigated because successful_check requires both receipts EXECUTED with matching input_manifest, so an unverified effect cannot reach completion. Residue: an unresolved set by a failed release or assess lets the task complete with unreconciled coordinator/risk state.
findings.falsifier: Trip unresolved via a failing harness_release, then call harness_finish with valid build/test receipts: it proceeds.
findings.bounded_fix: Apply the same guard to harness_finish, or document in the module header why finish is deliberately exempt.

findings.title: grant equality is order-sensitive inside nested objects and reports nothing useful
findings.detail: same_object is order-insensitive at the top level but compares nested values with structural equality on value.Value, whose Object is List(#(String,Value)). Semantically identical tasks[] entries with different key order compare unequal. Fail-closed and therefore safe, but any re-serialization by a different writer breaks activation with the single opaque message grant_differs_from_reviewed_proposal. Related low note: validate_review:179 reads review_sha256 from the grant and :202 sets that same value into expected, so that key's equality is a tautology; the real binding lives entirely in check:211.
findings.falsifier: Reorder the keys inside tasks[0] of the grant without changing content: activation fails with grant_differs_from_reviewed_proposal and no field named.
findings.bounded_fix: Make the comparison structural-recursive with key-set semantics and return the first differing key path.

findings.title: harness_clock skips grant revalidation
findings.detail: harness_clock calls clock.observe() directly while every other tool re-runs a.check. A clock read still answers after the grant expires or its file changes.
findings.falsifier: Expire the grant, then call harness_clock: it succeeds while harness_status fails.
findings.bounded_fix: Route harness_clock through a.check like harness_status, or document the exemption.

findings.title: sa-plan task claim takes an unbounded duration with no sanity ceiling (reviewer incident, preserved)
where: tools/sa-plan task claim WORKER PLAN LEASE_NS TASK_ID
findings.detail: This reviewer passed an absolute epoch-ns timestamp where LEASE_NS is a duration. Result: lease_until_ns 3577964911517363985 = 2083-05-19T15:08:31Z, a 56.7-year lease, accepted silently. Released and reclaimed at root's instruction with LEASE_NS=3600000000000: now attempt 2, lease_until_ns 1788983456875493482 = 2026-09-09T19:50:56Z, 60.0 minutes. 'sa-plan help task' documents the parameter only as LEASE_NS, which reads equally as a deadline.
findings.falsifier: tools/sa-plan task claim W PLAN $(date +%s%N) TASK stores a lease decades in the future without complaint.
findings.bounded_fix: Reject a duration above a policy ceiling (24h) and rename the CLI parameter LEASE_DURATION_NS.

findings.title: preflight FAIL at review time, unrelated to v9
findings.detail: FAIL (1 of 31): 2 untracked, first tools/telegram_client.cmi. OCaml build intermediates from concurrent Telegram work, not v9 source. Reported and NOT tidied: SC-WORKSPACE-ISO-001 INV-WS-02 makes another session's artifacts an incident to report rather than clean.
findings.bounded_fix: Owner of the Telegram work removes the intermediates or gitignores them.
